## 1. Get ACS data
Load the packages and define the ACS variables once. Download tract-level ACS 5-year data for Philadelphia County for the 2006–2010 and 2013-2017 period.
```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(tidycensus)

poverty_vars <- c(
  below_poverty = "B17001_002",
  total = "B17001_001"
)

acs_2010 <- get_acs(
  geography = "tract",
  variables = poverty_vars,
  state = 42,
  county = 101,
  year = 2010,
  survey = "acs5",
  output = "wide"
)

acs_2017 <- get_acs(
  geography = "tract",
  variables = poverty_vars,
  state = 42,
  county = 101,
  year = 2017,
  survey = "acs5",
  output = "wide"
)
```

## 2. Compute poverty rate and MOE for both periods, then pivot wide
Compute the poverty rate and its margin of error for 2006–2010 and 2013-2017 then combine and pivot wide. If `totalE` is missing or zero, set the rate and MOE to `NA` instead of producing invalid values.
```{r}
poverty_2010 <- acs_2010 %>%
  mutate(
    period = "2006_2010",
    poverty_rate = below_povertyE / totalE,
    poverty_rate_moe = moe_prop(
      below_povertyE,
      totalE,
      below_povertyM,
      totalM
    )
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    poverty_rate = if_else(totalE > 0, poverty_rate, NA_real_),
    poverty_rate_moe = if_else(totalE > 0, poverty_rate_moe, NA_real_)
  ) %>%
  select(GEOID, NAME, period, poverty_rate, poverty_rate_moe)

poverty_2017 <- acs_2017 %>%
  mutate(
    period = "2013_2017",
    poverty_rate = below_povertyE / totalE,
    poverty_rate_moe = moe_prop(
      below_povertyE,
      totalE,
      below_povertyM,
      totalM
    )
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    poverty_rate = if_else(totalE > 0, poverty_rate, NA_real_),
    poverty_rate_moe = if_else(totalE > 0, poverty_rate_moe, NA_real_)
  ) %>%
  select(GEOID, NAME, period, poverty_rate, poverty_rate_moe)

poverty_change <- bind_rows(
  poverty_2010,
  poverty_2017
)

poverty_wide <- poverty_change %>%
  select(GEOID, NAME, period, poverty_rate, poverty_rate_moe) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from  = period,
    values_from = c(poverty_rate, poverty_rate_moe)
  )
```


## 3. Calculate the change and CV
Calculate the change in poverty rate, the standard error of the difference, the difference MOE, the z-score, and whether the change is statistically detectable at the 90% confidence level. Calculate the coefficient of variation for each period and classify each estimate as reliable, somewhat reliable, or unreliable.
```{r}
poverty_tested <- poverty_wide %>%
  mutate(
    change   = poverty_rate_2013_2017 -
               poverty_rate_2006_2010,
    se_1     = poverty_rate_moe_2006_2010 / 1.645,
    se_2     = poverty_rate_moe_2013_2017 / 1.645,
    se_diff  = sqrt(se_1^2 + se_2^2),
    moe_diff = se_diff * 1.645,
    z        = change / se_diff,
    significant = abs(z) > 1.645
  )

poverty_tested <- poverty_tested %>%
  mutate(
    cv_2006_2010 = se_1 / poverty_rate_2006_2010 * 100,
    cv_2013_2017 = se_2 / poverty_rate_2013_2017 * 100,
    reliability_2006_2010 = 
      case_when(
        cv_2006_2010 < 12 ~ "reliable",
        cv_2006_2010 <= 40 ~ "somewhat reliable",
        TRUE ~ "unreliable"
      ),
    reliability_2013_2017 = 
      case_when(
        cv_2013_2017 < 12 ~ "reliable",
        cv_2013_2017 <= 40 ~ "somewhat reliable",
        TRUE ~ "unreliable"
      )
  )
```

## 4. Deal with NA data and report missingness
Summarize how many tracts have missing changes or missing significance results. This keeps the missing-data step explicit instead of silently dropping observations. Keep only tracts with valid change, valid difference MOE, and a positive standard error of the difference. These are the cases used for the change plot, reliability summaries, and histogram.
```{r}
poverty_tested %>%
  summarise(
    total_tracts   = n(),
    missing_change = sum(is.na(change)),
    missing_moe    = sum(is.na(moe_diff)),
    missing_z      = sum(is.na(z)),
    missing_sig    = sum(is.na(significant)),
    detectable     = sum(significant, na.rm = TRUE),
    not_detectable = sum(!significant, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

poverty_complete <- poverty_tested %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(change),
    !is.na(moe_diff),
    !is.na(se_diff),
    se_diff > 0
  )
```

## 5. Check the result
```{r}
poverty_tested %>%
  select(
    GEOID, NAME, 
    poverty_rate_2006_2010,
    poverty_rate_2013_2017,
    change, moe_diff, z, significant
  )

poverty_tested %>%
  count(significant)
```

## 6. Plot the change in poverty rate (most unreliable 15)
Plot the change in poverty rate across Philadelphia census tracts. Error bars show the 90% MOE of the change. Some tracts showed extreme MOE, and the x axis label is horrible!
```{r}
poverty_plot <- poverty_complete %>%
  mutate(
    change_pp = change * 100,
    moe_diff_pp = moe_diff * 100,
    moe_pct = if_else(change == 0, Inf, moe_diff / abs(change) * 100),
    NAME = str_remove(NAME, "Census Tract ") %>%
      str_remove(", Philadelphia County, Pennsylvania")
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(moe_pct)) %>%
  slice_head(n = 15)

ggplot(
  poverty_plot,
  aes(x = reorder(NAME, change_pp), y = change_pp)
) +
  geom_col(aes(fill = change_pp > 0)) +
  geom_errorbar(
    aes(ymin = change_pp - moe_diff_pp,
        ymax = change_pp + moe_diff_pp),
    width = 0.3
  ) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    x = NULL,
    y = "Change in poverty rate (percentage points)",
    title = "15 most unreliable poverty-rate changes",
    subtitle = "2013–2017 ACS5 minus 2006–2010 ACS5; error bars show 90% MOE"
  )
```

## 7. Summarize reliability
Create a reliability table for the two periods. Missing reliability values are labeled explicitly as `missing/undefined`.
```{r}
reliability_table <- poverty_tested %>%
  select(
    GEOID, reliability_2006_2010, reliability_2013_2017
  ) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(reliability_2006_2010, reliability_2013_2017),
    names_to = "period",
    values_to = "reliability"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    reliability = replace_na(reliability, "missing/undefined")
  ) %>%
  count(period, reliability)

reliability_table
```

## 8. Plot the distribution of poverty-rate changes
Plot the distribution of changes across Philadelphia census tracts using complete cases only.
```{r}
ggplot(
  poverty_complete %>%
    mutate(change_pp = change * 100),
  aes(x = change_pp)
) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 30) +
  geom_vline(
    xintercept = 0,
    linetype = "dashed"
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Change in poverty rate (percentage points)",
    y = "Number of census tracts",
    title = "Distribution of poverty-rate changes across Philadelphia",
    subtitle = "2013–2017 ACS5 minus 2006–2010 ACS5"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```
